intro: Inverse-CDF sampling maps uniform draws into categories with prescribed probabilities. Supplying the draws makes the transformation deterministic and testable.
task: Build a categorical CDF and choose the first cumulative mass strictly above each supplied draw.
requirements: probabilities is a probability vector. draws is a vector of fixed real numbers in [0,1). Do not generate random values.
Return {"cdf": cumulative masses, "indices": first index whose cumulative mass is strictly greater than each draw}.
Force the last cumulative value to exactly one after normalizing accepted probabilities. Zero-mass categories must never be selected.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

examples.output:

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Cumulative masses divide [0,1) into half-open category intervals.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: A right-sided search moves past equal cumulative boundaries and zero-width intervals.

explanation: Inverse-CDF sampling maps uniform draws into categories with prescribed probabilities. Supplying the draws makes the transformation deterministic and testable.
Strictly greater cumulative mass determines boundary behavior. A left-sided search can select a zero-probability category at a repeated cumulative boundary, so the convention matters.
